# A Conspiracy of Credit, Part III: How the Greatest Fraud in Human History Happened - and What It Means for Private Credit Today

First listed: 2026-05-21 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [Substack: A Conspiracy of Credit, Part III: How the Greatest Fraud in Human History Happened - and What It Means for Private Credit Today](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/a-conspiracy-of-credit-part-iii-how) - 2026-05-21

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Eisman explains securitization and mortgage-era due-diligence failures, then argues that software concentration, retail liquidity promises and insurer links create private-credit vulnerabilities. Documented underwriting misconduct supports his central historical concern, but several absolutes fail: MBS predates the 1980s, Denmark has a substantial 30-year fixed mortgage market, some due-diligence samples expanded, and consumer mortgages can be modified. Civil RMBS enforcement contradicts broad claims that nothing happened without settling particular criminal-referral outcomes. The 2027-2028 refinancing scenario remains unfinished; universal private-software valuation losses and undated credit-cycle predictions remain unproved.

Substantive article review with paragraph references. Distinguishes persuasive mechanisms from overgeneralized history, unverified market estimates, normative judgments and actual future deadlines. The specific criminal-accountability claim remains unresolved rather than rebutted with unrelated originator cases.

## Material claims

<a id="article-202840159-c001"></a>
### 001. The US has the largest, deepest fixed-income market entirely because of securitization.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at Paragraphs 4, 5](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/a-conspiracy-of-credit-part-iii-how) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The exclusive causal attribution is not demonstrated; sovereign issuance, institutional savings and legal infrastructure also require examination.

Assessment test: Compare market size consistently and isolate securitization from other causes.


<a id="article-202840159-c002"></a>
### 002. European and other economies rely primarily on banks for corporate debt while US companies have more developed capital-market alternatives.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at Paragraphs 5](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/a-conspiracy-of-credit-part-iii-how) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

No matched cross-country corporate funding dataset was inspected.

Assessment test: Compare bank loans, bonds and private credit on common definitions.


<a id="article-202840159-c003"></a>
### 003. Securitization pools loans and sells claims on their cash flows, allowing originators to recycle funds and broadening investor access.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at Paragraphs 6, 10](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/a-conspiracy-of-credit-part-iii-how) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The joint official report describes loan pooling, security issuance and recycling of origination capacity.

Assessment test: Separate funding access from the quality and distribution of risk.

- [Enhancing disclosure in mortgage-backed securities markets](https://www.sec.gov/news/studies/mortgagebacked.htm) (2003-01): Modern MBS began with Ginnie Mae in 1970, Freddie Mac in 1971 and private Bank of America issuance in 1977; Fannie issuance began in 1981. Guarantees and eligibility varied. Loan sales recycle lending capacity.

<a id="article-202840159-c004"></a>

**Wrong** | Steve Eisman | material factual premise | supporting

[Source at Paragraphs 8](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/a-conspiracy-of-credit-part-iii-how) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Modern agency MBS began in 1970 and private issuance in 1977, before the claimed creation date. His development role does not establish invention.

Assessment test: Distinguish popularization from the first issuance.

- [Enhancing disclosure in mortgage-backed securities markets](https://www.sec.gov/news/studies/mortgagebacked.htm) (2003-01): Modern MBS began with Ginnie Mae in 1970, Freddie Mac in 1971 and private Bank of America issuance in 1977; Fannie issuance began in 1981. <a id="article-202840159-c008"></a>
### 008. The US is the only country with a robust 30-year fixed-rate mortgage market; every other country uses variable rates.

<a id="article-202840159-c009"></a>
### 009. The US 30-year fixed-rate product exists entirely because of mortgage securitization.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at Paragraphs 11](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/a-conspiracy-of-credit-part-iii-how) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The absolute counterfactual is not established by the financing mechanism.

Assessment test: Examine historical origination, portfolio lending, guarantees and alternative funding.


<a id="article-202840159-c010"></a>
### 010. Non-agency loan pools require credit enhancement to create senior securities protected from expected borrower losses.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at Paragraphs 13](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/a-conspiracy-of-credit-part-iii-how) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Subordinated claims absorb losses before senior claims under the specified waterfall.

Conditional reasoning: With pool loss L and subordinate principal S paid after senior claims, senior principal loss is max(0,L-S), ignoring expenses and timing shortfalls. Subordination protects senior claims only up to S.

Assessment test: Inspect actual priority, collateral, reserves and recovery terms.


<a id="article-202840159-c011"></a>
### 011. A first-loss equity tranche and successively senior debt tranches distribute credit losses unevenly across the same loan pool.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at Paragraphs 15, 16](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/a-conspiracy-of-credit-part-iii-how) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The stated building analogy describes a valid sequential-loss structure.

Conditional reasoning: If losses are allocated from junior to senior, each tranche loses only after all lower-ranking loss capacity is exhausted. This is a contractual allocation, not elimination of aggregate loss.

Assessment test: Use the actual deal waterfall, including interest diversion and triggers.


<a id="article-202840159-c012"></a>
### 012. A 70% senior tranche with 30% subordination can withstand the first 30% of principal losses in the simplified example.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at Paragraphs 16](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/a-conspiracy-of-credit-part-iii-how) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The example follows directly from the assumed loss waterfall.

Conditional reasoning: For 100 collateral and 30 subordinate principal, principal losses L<=30 leave 70 senior principal intact. For L>30, senior principal loss equals L-30 up to 70.

Assessment test: Include fees, timing and interest losses in an actual transaction.


<a id="article-202840159-c013"></a>
### 013. Higher junior coupons compensate investors for bearing earlier losses, while safer senior tranches can pay less.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at Paragraphs 15, 16](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/a-conspiracy-of-credit-part-iii-how) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

This is the directional risk-pricing mechanism under otherwise equal terms, rather than proof that illustrative 25% and 10% coupons were universal.

Qualification: The percentages are examples, not a dated market survey.

Conditional reasoning: For equal purchase prices and noncredit terms, a claim with larger expected losses needs larger promised payments to match another claim's expected payoff. Risk aversion may require an additional premium.

Assessment test: Compare expected losses, liquidity, optionality and actual prices.

Qualification: Do not convert an extreme pool outcome into an aggregate market loss rate.

Assessment test: Reconstruct vintage-level realized pool and tranche losses.

<a id="article-202840159-c026"></a>
### 026. Wall Street due-diligence failures and misleading underwriting disclosures provide concrete evidence of misconduct.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at Paragraphs 31, 35](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/a-conspiracy-of-credit-part-iii-how) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

FCIC evidence and Goldman's agreed facts document known exceptions and misleading representations. This does not establish every issuer's criminal liability.

- [Financial Crisis Inquiry Report, pages 165-169](https://fcic-static.law.stanford.edu/cdn_media/fcic-reports/fcic_final_report_full.pdf) (2011-01): Clayton classified 28% of sampled loans as deficient during January 2006-June 2007; 39% of those were waived in. Sampling methods varied. The report documents underwriting representations inconsistent with known exceptions, while not declaring every exception fraudulent.
- [Goldman Sachs agrees to pay more than $5 billion over RMBS](https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/goldman-sachs-agrees-pay-more-5-billion-connection-its-sale-residential-mortgage-backed) (2016-04-11): The $5.06 billion civil settlement and agreed facts document knowing underwriting misrepresentations and typically unexpanded due diligence. It preserved criminal liability and does not establish the disposition of a particular FCIC criminal referral.

Some clients expanded samples after poor results. Clayton had competitors and reviewed loans under consideration for purchase. Exceptions could be cured or supported by compensating factors.

### 043. Retail private-credit vehicles offer limited quarterly liquidity, and withdrawal demand has exceeded caps.

Qualification: Do not generalize these examples to every fund or treat gross requests as forced asset sales.

- [April 2026 shareholder update](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1812554/000119312526139036/d127449dex991.htm) (2026-04-02): Q1 requests were estimated at 21.9% of outstanding shares; fulfillment was capped at 5%. - [April 2026 shareholder update](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1869453/000119312526139035/d102817dex991.htm) (2026-04-02): Q1 tender requests were estimated at 40.7% of shares; the fund fulfilled a 5% offer pro rata. Management links investor concern to AI/software exposure while asserting continuing portfolio performance.

<a id="article-202840159-c048"></a>
### 048. Private-equity software assets are worth at best half their acquisition prices because public comparables have compressed.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at Paragraphs 48](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/a-conspiracy-of-credit-part-iii-how) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Comparable repricing may lower marks, but it cannot establish a universal 50% ceiling without earnings growth, debt and enterprise-versus-equity adjustments.

Conditional reasoning: Enterprise value equals multiple times the relevant earnings measure. A 50% multiple decline leaves value unchanged if earnings double. Equity value equals enterprise value minus net debt, so a public equity-price change is not a universal private enterprise-value change.

Assessment test: Value each asset using current cash flows, debt and appropriate comparable multiples.

<a id="article-202840159-c054"></a>
### 054. Corporate debt can be restructured, whereas consumer loans cannot and had no modification mechanism during the housing crisis.

**Wrong** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at Paragraphs 51](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/a-conspiracy-of-credit-part-iii-how) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Treasury's HAMP explicitly created mortgage modifications and payment reductions. Scale and servicing frictions do not mean impossibility.

Assessment test: Compare legal mechanisms, capacity, take-up and modification outcomes.

- [Home Affordable Modification Program](https://home.treasury.gov/data/troubled-assets-relief-program/housing/mha/hamp) (accessed 2026-11-10): HAMP provided a mechanism for mortgage servicers to modify distressed homeowners loans and reduce monthly payments. Initial servicing constraints did not make consumer restructuring impossible.

<a id="article-202840159-c055"></a>
### 055. Corporate borrowers can simply elect payment-in-kind interest or maturity extensions to defer distress.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at Paragraphs 51](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/a-conspiracy-of-credit-part-iii-how) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

These are possible contractual tools, but unilateral election requires existing rights; otherwise creditor consent is needed.

Conditional reasoning: A contract requiring cash interest and repayment on date T is not satisfied by unilaterally adding interest to principal or paying after T. PIK or extension is effective only if the contract permits it or the required parties amend it.

Assessment test: Inspect covenants, PIK options, amendment thresholds and cash-flow sustainability.

Initial servicing constraints did not make consumer restructuring impossible.

## Framework and tools

- Trace cash flows and loss seniority through securitization.
- Separate collateral risk from repackaged security notional.
- Inspect sampling design before extrapolating defects.
- Distinguish civil enforcement from specific criminal referrals.
- Match liquidity promises to underlying loan liquidity.
- Separate public equity prices from private enterprise values.
- Track maturity cohorts and sponsor equity support.
- Include affiliated insurers in exposure mapping.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Illustrative 100-unit loan-pool tranche waterfall
- Clayton due-diligence samples and underwriting exceptions
- Public software valuation comparisons
- 2027-2028 refinancing percentages
- Quarterly redemption caps
- Private-credit market-size estimates

## Source cautions

Signed solo article by Steve Eisman. No guest attribution or inferred dialogue.
- This source is the complete substantive signed-in article, not an episode transcript. No player or full video transcript was available.
- Use paragraph_references and source_locator; the normalization placeholders at zero are not speech timestamps.
- Illustrative building and coupon figures are not treated as universal historical deal statistics.
- The criminal-accountability discussion concerns Wall Street due-diligence conduct; scope is preserved.
- Market-size, software and maturity estimates lack identified original datasets in the article.
